clue.text: Subway at first rates No.1 for sandwiches

parts.note: number one is a jokey way of referring to oneself, me

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold something between two layers, so these pieces close round the next

parts.note: for can mean to, as in a present for or to someone

indicators.note: at first signals that only the opening letter of rates is used

explanation.surface: An underground railway is said to lead the ratings at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' has the pronoun and the preposition close round the opening letter of 'rates'; 'No.1' is a jokey way of saying oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Metro is the usual name for an underground railway system in Paris and many other cities.

clue.text: Players at Belgrade Theatre's premier singer

parts.note: Red Star Belgrade is the famous Serbian football club, so its players are Red Star

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the first letter of Theatre's is wanted

explanation.surface: A lead singer at Belgrade's theatre, with actors in the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'Theatre' paint a stage, but the players are the footballers of Red Star Belgrade, and the singer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird, and crosswords often call any songbird a singer.

clue.text: Amount of ale editor's finally consumed goes to press

indicators.note: consumed as in swallowed, so the beer measure takes a letter inside it

parts.note: ale is served in pints

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of editor's

explanation.surface: An editor drinks some beer before the newspaper is printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' puts R, the final letter of 'editor's', inside PINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To print a newspaper is to send it to press, so goes to press is a synonym.

clue.text: Barney violently ejected

definitions.meaning: barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel
the past tense of spit, to force out of the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone called Barney was thrown out by force.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNEY is everyday British slang for a row or squabble; the capital letter makes it look like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, and spat also means spit out forcefully.

clue.text: Where multiplier is losing touch with Jones and family?

definitions.meaning: in a sum such as 2 times 3 the multiplier comes after the times sign

definitions.text: losing touch with Jones and family?
definitions.meaning: failing to keep up with the Joneses, the neighbours whose lifestyle one tries to match, is being old-fashioned

explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a British newspaper, one of the puzzle's many papers. 'Keeping up with the Joneses' is the idiom for matching the neighbours' possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of date or old-fashioned means not keeping pace with modern trends.

clue.text: Using electronic communications without ID — unlike this puzzle

definitions.meaning: an office that works this way deals in e-mails and digital files rather than paper
papers are identity documents, and this puzzle is full of newspapers

explanation.surface: Someone going digital and carrying no identification, in contrast to a grid full of newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is newspapers: about thirteen entries are paper titles, so this puzzle is far from paperless.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperless describes work done without paper documents, and also a person lacking identity papers.

clue.text: See 18
Turkish dish girlfriend's brought west on stern of junk

indicators.note: a stern is the rear of a ship, so this takes the last letter of junk
in an across clue moving west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: babe is a slang term of endearment for a girlfriend

explanation.surface: A girlfriend fetches a Turkish meal aboard a Chinese sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought west' reverses the girlfriend in this across answer, and 'stern of' takes the end of 'junk', a Chinese sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Kebabs, pieces of meat grilled on a skewer, are a classic dish of Turkish cuisine.

clue.text: Say which we collectively enjoy

parts.note: having a say is the influence the public wields together, popular political pressure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the noun, a voice in decisions; THE PEOPLE is a British Sunday newspaper, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means the political influence exerted by the public acting together, as in mass protests.

clue.text: Up to nothing in Paris, son's bored

indicators.note: bored as in drilled into, so son makes a hole in the French phrase and sits inside

parts.note: in French à rien means to nothing
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son in Paris is bored, with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' puts S inside A RIEN. 'son's' means son has, not son is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has arisen has got up, so the past participle can stand for up, as in 'he is up'.

clue.text: See 5
Car brand new and jack out, just notice wheels!

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn round, so the whole sequence is read backwards
out means taken away, so the letter for jack leaves the word just

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack on playing cards
an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging us to look at the wheels of a new car with the jack removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the card letter for jack from 'just', and 'wheels' turns the whole string round; the exclamation mark makes it read like an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Datsun was the name under which the Japanese maker Nissan sold its cars abroad.

clue.text: Buffalo seen here after antelope

parts.note: Buffalo is a city in New York State, abbreviated NY
à la, French for in the style of, means after, as in a painting after Rembrandt

explanation.surface: Buffalo roam in a place where antelope have already been spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo' looks like the animal beside the antelope, but it is the city in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope of the bushbuck family.

clue.text: Sell bike to receiver?

indicators.note: the receiver is the listener, so the word is as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to bike is to cycle, to pedal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to sell a bicycle to a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: A receiver is also a fence, someone who takes stolen goods, which is the surface's reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to sell goods, typically by going from place to place hawking them.

clue.text: High-pitch sound attracting fast runner — so it did for Hamelin's rats

parts.note: a pip is a short high-pitched tone, like the radio time signal
the emu is a flightless bird that runs fast
sic, Latin for so or thus, marks a quotation as given

explanation.surface: A shrill note draws a sprinter, just as the piper's tune lured the rats of Hamelin.
explanation.walkthrough: In the story of the Pied Piper of Hamelin, the piper's tune leads the town's rats away to drown.
explanation.definitionFit: The piper's music is what lured the rats of Hamelin to their end, so it did for them.

clue.text: Present head of Gestapo with papers

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of Gestapo

parts.note: two newspapers: the i and the FT, the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Presenting a Gestapo chief with documents.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'papers' are two British newspapers, the i and the Financial Times, in keeping with the newspaper theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a present, something given freely to another person.

clue.text: See 26
Get distorted from detailing complex mixed images on screen

definitions.note: an inlaid screen has pictures set into it in mixed materials such as wood and shell

indicators.note: complex as in intricately mixed, so the letters of detailing are rearranged
distorted means the letters of get are scrambled too before they are taken out

explanation.surface: Instructions about images on a computer screen getting distorted by complex detailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges DETAILING; take out the letters of 'Get' ('distorted', so in any order) and the remaining six letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid work such as marquetry sets pieces of different materials into a surface to form pictures.

clue.text: Word from backwoodsmen?

parts.note: word here means news, passed along informally by people in the remote countryside

explanation.walkthrough: The TELEGRAPH is a British newspaper, part of the theme; the bush is remote wild country.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an informal grapevine by which rumours and news spread rapidly.

clue.text: Plant something ruby-coloured in ring to produce this reaction?

definitions.meaning: the plant meant is a tall reed of marshes, also spelt with one L

definitions.text: something ruby-coloured in ring to produce this reaction?
definitions.meaning: a red cape waved in the bullring makes the bull charge

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as BULL RUSH: the charge a matador provokes in the ring with his red cape.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulrush, or bullrush, is a tall waterside plant also called reedmace.

clue.text: Send over third note, counter tracking packages

indicators.note: packages as in wraps up, so the track encloses the reversed note

parts.note: a rail is the track a train runs on

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the note is read backwards

parts.note: in doh ray me, me is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A post office counter sends on a third letter while tracking parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' reverses the sol-fa note and 'packages' wraps the track round it; the surface suggests a post office counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To remail something is to post it again, sending it over once more.

clue.text: Scrape off second slice of daily bread, dropping middle onto floor

indicators.note: the second slice of daily is its second letter
in a down clue the floor is the bottom, so the central letter of bread falls to the end

explanation.surface: Instructions to scrape the second slice of the daily loaf after dropping it on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second slice of' picks a letter of 'daily'; 'dropping middle onto floor' sends the centre letter of 'bread' to the bottom of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away or scrape off a surface by rubbing.

clue.text: See 24
Players natter about rising alternative rock band

indicators.note: about as in surrounding, so the chat word goes round the band

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly, to natter

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: R.E.M. was the American alternative rock band

explanation.surface: Musicians chatter about the rise of an indie rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the band upwards in this down answer and 'about' wraps the chatter word round it; R.E.M. were the American band.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamers are people who play computer games, so they are players.

clue.text: See 9
Having knocked back ace narcotic, granny sets about a group of vigilantes

indicators.note: about means the long string of pieces goes around the a from the clue
knocked back, as a drink is swallowed, here means turned backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent or first-rate, like ace; the 1 is written as I
a narcotic is a drug
nan is an informal name for a grandmother
a jelly gels when it sets

explanation.surface: A grandmother who has taken drugs lays into a band of citizen patrollers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses ace and narcotic together, giving GURDIA, and 'about' wraps the whole string round A. A1, written AI, means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian Angels are a volunteer anti-crime patrol founded in New York in 1979.

clue.text: Caught by then?

parts.note: something caught is held in a net
by can mean times, as in 3 by 4, written as X

explanation.walkthrough: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in measurements such as 6 by 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Next and then both mean afterwards, at the following moment in a sequence.

clue.text: Is it 11 for Roman 9?

parts.note: the Roman numeral for 11 is XI, which is 9, IX, flipped left to right

explanation.walkthrough: The MIRROR is a British tabloid newspaper, and the i is another, both part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflection reverses left and right, as XI is IX seen in a looking glass.

clue.text: Nervous of snakes?

definitions.meaning: British slang for frightened or nervous
snakes wind, twisting and bending as they go

explanation.walkthrough: Windy for scared is British slang, from being 'in the wind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervous person is described as windy, and a twisting route is windy too.

clue.text: Leader-writer that was forced out?

parts.note: ex means former, that was once
a leader is a newspaper's main opinion article, written by a press editor

explanation.surface: An editorial writer who was sacked from the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EX-PRESS ED, a former newspaper editor; the EXPRESS is also a British paper in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice expressed from fruit is squeezed or pressed out of it.
